motivation: EgoConseq-Bench evaluates whether a vision-language model can infer the visible local physical consequence of its own body executing a short action from one egocentric RGB image. It is not navigation, generic spatial relations, object physics, or hidden-space inference; it isolates body-conditioned ego swept-volume consequence reasoning.
design_principles: Single-image ego-action VQA: one RGB frame, one body description, one action primitive, one answer.
Body is a query-conditioned causal collision operator: do(body=r) can flip the consequence on the same image and action.
Distances are normalized by body width, with 1 body-width = 2r, avoiding absolute monocular metric claims.
Labels come from deterministic swept-cylinder geometry and visibility filtering, not LLM judgment.
Core cases must be visible or directly inferable from the current egocentric RGB/depth render: no hidden-corner, off-image, or occluded decisive geometry.
Counterfactual body/action pairs, blind controls, option balancing, and shortcut heuristics are mandatory validity checks.
Swept-cylinder collision is the label engine, not the novelty claim; novelty is the isolated diagnostic of MLLM embodied consequence grounding.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-width forward swept extent
inspired_by: Prior spatial benchmarks only as motivation-to-QA design examples
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Reads how far the queried cylindrical body can move forward before first visible collision, normalized by body width.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible directional swept-volume comparison
inspired_by: VSI-Bench / Thinking in Space only as methodology inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares candidate visible sweeps in small egocentric angles without relying on route planning or hidden space.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Short composite ego-action consequence
inspired_by: MindCube only as what-if QA construction inspiration, not hidden-space reasoning
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares a small turn-then-forward consequence with straight motion under the same visible-local swept-volume boundary.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-intervention consequence
inspired_by: Counterfactual QA methodology only; the intervention is EgoConseq's do(body=r) collision operator
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Holds image and action fixed while changing radius to test embodiment-sensitive consequence flips and no-flip controls.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible fixed-horizon passability
inspired_by: Prior benchmarks only as coverage-design precedent
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Asks whether a visible forward swept corridor is contact-free for the queried body, without semantic object-physics claims.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward. How many body-widths can it move before first contact? Options: <2, 2-4, 4-8, >8.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute forward max_safe_distance_body_widths on the radius-specific navmesh and bin into <2 / 2-4 / 4-8 / >8; require visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, collision_point_visible when applicable, and bin_margin_body_widths>=0.5.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Candidate directions: left-front {theta} degrees, straight, right-front {theta} degrees. Rank them by maximum distance before first contact, longest to shortest.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute swept distances for {-theta,0,+theta}, sort descending, and discard near-tie rankings unless the separation margin is sufficient; theta defaults to 30 degrees with 15 degrees allowed.

tasks.question_template: Same RGB and action: move straight forward for {horizon} body-widths, where each body-width equals that body's diameter. Body A radius {r_a} m and Body B radius {r_b} m, height 1.5 m. Which bodies complete the action without contact? Options: both bodies, only Body A, only Body B, neither body.
tasks.answer_derivation: At the same pose/action/horizon, compare passability across radius-specific navmeshes; randomize body order; generate flip and no-flip controls with counterfactual_group_id and flip_pair_id.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Compare A) move straight forward and B) rotate {theta} degrees, then move forward. Which action allows more body-widths before first contact? Options: A, B, about the same.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compare straight max distance with turn-then-forward max distance; label about the same only within a fixed tie margin of 0.5 body-width. Extension-only until FOV support is verified.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move forward for {horizon} body-widths within the currently visible region. Is the swept body contact-free? Options: yes, no.
tasks.answer_derivation: Check whether every swept sample through the fixed horizon remains navigable for the radius-specific body. Extension-only until hidden-geometry and shortcut risks are audited.

qa_design.name: Body-Width Forward Horizon
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask how many body widths the queried cylindrical body can move straight forward before first visible contact.

qa_design.name: Visible Directional Sweep Ranking
qa_design.question_pattern: Rank left-front, straight, and right-front swept distances within the current FOV.

qa_design.name: Composite Motion Consequence
qa_design.question_pattern: Compare straight motion with a small turn-then-forward action under the same body constraints.

qa_design.name: Body Counterfactual Sweep
qa_design.question_pattern: Hold RGB and action fixed while changing body radius, then ask which bodies complete the sweep.
qa_design.answer_space: both / only Body A / only Body B / neither

qa_design.name: Visible Passability
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask whether a fixed forward swept horizon in the visible region is contact-free for the queried body.

novelty_positioning: EgoConseq is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned consequence VQA; it is not route navigation, active exploration, or long-horizon planning.
The benchmark does not claim novel collision geometry; swept-cylinder intersection is the deterministic label engine.
Compared with PhysBench, it asks about the ego body rather than object or scene physics.
Compared with CapNav, it is one-step visible-local consequence reasoning rather than route-level capability-conditioned navigation.
Compared with TouchSafeBench, it uses a hypothetical action from single RGB rather than multi-view/current collision grounding.
Compared with ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench, it isolates body-width swept-volume collision/passability rather than broad affordance or scene-state evolution.
VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and related spatial-intelligence benchmarks are cited only for benchmark-design discipline and adjacent positioning, not for importing their QA categories.

findings.claim: The strongest CVPR/ICLR diagnostic contribution is isolating ego-body action consequence grounding from navigation, object physics, and generic spatial relations.
findings.evidence: goal.md defines one RGB frame, one body, one action primitive, and labels from Body x Action_trajectory intersecting scene geometry within visible/local evidence.

findings.claim: T1, T2, and T4 should be the core demo families.
findings.evidence: T1 tests body-normalized metric extent, T2 tests directional/configurational sweep comparison, and T4 directly tests do(body=r) counterfactual flips for H3.

findings.claim: T3 and T5 are useful but should remain extension tasks until visibility probes pass.
findings.evidence: Turn-then-forward consequences and binary passability are more exposed to hidden-geometry leakage and simple yes/no or center-ray shortcuts.

findings.claim: The QA taxonomy should be derived from EgoConseq's own swept-volume readouts: metric extent, directional comparison, short action simulation, body intervention, and fixed-horizon passability.
findings.evidence: VSI-Bench/Thinking in Space and MindCube are useful methodological references for aligning QA types to validity claims, but their video memory, cognitive-map, and hidden-space tasks should not be imported.

findings.claim: Near-neighbor contrast must stay narrow and explicit.
findings.evidence: PhysBench covers broad physical world/object-scene understanding; CapNav is route-level capability-conditioned navigation; TouchSafeBench is multi-view/current or imminent collision grounding; ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench evaluate egocentric world/action-sequence prediction rather than single-step ego-body sweep consequences.

findings.claim: All five tasks are feasible in principle under swept-cylinder/navmesh labeling if the generator emits oracle, visibility, margin, and counterfactual metadata.
findings.evidence: Habitat-Sim supports configurable agents and sensors, and HM3D/MP3D provide indoor geometry suitable for deterministic RGB/depth rendering and navmesh-based collision queries.

findings.claim: Current showcase readiness is not proven by the input manifest.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path:null and data_manifest:null, while coverage counts refer to drafted cases with zero reviewed_counts.

findings.claim: The current phase can support illustrative case drafting but not simulator-validated showcase claims.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json reports data_manifest_path:null and data_manifest:null while blackboard.phase is showcase.

findings.claim: Coverage should remain broad across the five EgoConseq readouts.
findings.evidence: goal.md defines T1 forward horizon, T2 directional ranking, T3 turn-then-forward comparison, T4 body counterfactual, and T5 visible passability as readouts of the same swept-volume formula.

findings.claim: T1, T2, and T4 remain the most important demo cases; T3 and T5 should be shown as extension coverage.
findings.evidence: The design_doc in the manifest marks T1/T2/T4 as core_demo_tasks and T3/T5 as extension_tasks.

findings.claim: Current cases cannot support benchmark validity claims.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json reports data_manifest_path=null and data_manifest=null; blackboard/state.json reports 50 total cases, all in needs_revision and 0 surviving.

findings.claim: All drafted cases are visually unjudgeable as illustrative benchmark examples.
findings.evidence: Case visibility fields use assumptions such as visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7 or requires_hidden_geometry=false, but no case includes rgb_path, depth_path, sweep_overlay_path, collision_point_visible, bin_margin, fov_supported, or oracle_trace_path values.

findings.claim: The showcase requirements are necessary but insufficient.
findings.evidence: The frozen design requires oracle/visibility fields, but there is no gate requiring non-null realized values, T2/T3 ranking margins, heuristic-baseline failure, or human agreement before a case can be shown.

findings.claim: The empirical assumptions in goal.md remain unproven.
findings.evidence: No M1/M2b/M4/M5/human results are present, so H1 oracle gap, H2 blind near-random behavior, and H3 body-counterfactual sensitivity are still claims, not evidence.

findings.claim: The drafted cases are shortcut-solvable without ego-body swept-volume reasoning.
findings.evidence: T1 can reduce to center-depth or corridor-length bins; T2 to largest visible floor patch or side priors; T3 to action-angle priors; T4 to monotonic smaller-body rules; T5 to binary radius/passability priors.

findings.claim: Nominal task coverage exists, but evidence coverage has over-narrowed to template-level collision/passability.
findings.evidence: The case store has 10 cases each for T1-T5, but every answer is a text draft rather than a rendered single-image consequence instance tied to geometry.

findings.claim: Freeze T1, T2, and T4 as the current core demo/showcase task families; keep T3 and T5 as extension families until visibility and shortcut gates pass.
findings.evidence: goal.md prioritizes T1/T2/T4 for the demo; paper_designer also recommends T1/T2/T4 core and T3/T5 extension.

findings.claim: The public taxonomy should be EgoConseq readouts, not imported spatial-intelligence categories.
findings.evidence: goal.md defines all tasks as readouts of Body x Action trajectory intersecting visible scene geometry; paper_designer states VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, and MindCube are only methodology inspiration.

findings.claim: No current illustrative case should be marked show in the HTML showcase.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path:null and data_manifest:null; case_author cases use visibility fields that say Assumes rather than reporting rgb_path, depth_path, sweep_overlay_path, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, fov_supported, or oracle_trace_path.

findings.claim: All current answers, visibility statements, and rationale fields must be marked not simulator-validated.
findings.evidence: case_author explicitly says the cases are drafts only; expert_reviewer confirms no M1/M2b/M4/M5/human numbers and no simulator-backed case manifest are present.

findings.claim: Do not claim H1, H2, H3, validity-gate success, or showcase readiness yet.
findings.evidence: No oracle accuracy, blind baseline, VLM baseline, human sanity, or counterfactual-pair consistency results are attached.

recommendations: Freeze the paper demo core as T1/T2/T4; keep T3/T5 optional until deterministic visibility probes pass.
Keep case_generation_spec.status as proposed in this designer output; only the arbiter should freeze it.
Treat current text-authored cases as templates only until simulator-backed oracle fields and visualization paths are attached.
Make case_author emit oracle metadata, visibility metrics, margins, counterfactual IDs, and asset paths so HTML review is useful before full baseline validation.
Use prior spatial-intelligence benchmarks only as examples of motivation-to-QA discipline, not as task-taxonomy templates.
Gate paper claims on M4 oracle high accuracy, M5 near chance, strongest VLM well below oracle, and human/geometric annotators above VLM.
Use these 50 cases as human-readable template seeds, not accepted benchmark samples.
Attach RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, visibility metrics, and counterfactual IDs before showcase review.
Prioritize simulator generation for T1/T2/T4 first, then retain T3/T5 only where visible-local validity passes.
Adjudicate this phase as needs_case_generation, not ready_for_showcase_review.

Minimal pilot to continue: at least 60 sim-validated core cases across T1/T2/T4, M4 oracle >=95%, M5 near chance, strongest VLM clearly below oracle and humans, and H3 flip-pair failure above human/oracle error.
Do not accept any placeholder case into the showcase until RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, visibility metrics, margins, and counterfactual IDs are attached.
For T2/T3, require a numeric separation margin between alternatives; otherwise rank/about-same labels become arbitrary.
For T1, freeze bins only after survey histograms and reject cases within 0.5 body-width of bin boundaries.
For T4, report counterfactual-pair consistency in addition to per-question accuracy.
For T5, keep as extension unless binary passability beats radius-only and centerline heuristics by a meaningful margin.
Stop or redesign if blind/radius/2D heuristics approach VLM performance or if humans cannot reliably judge the audited cases from RGB plus allowed overlays.
Next artifact: produce a simulator-backed data_manifest.json with at least 20 T1, 20 T2, and 20 T4 core cases, plus optional T3/T5 only after visibility gates pass.
Attach RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, label, margins, visibility metadata, ambiguity fields, and counterfactual IDs for every case.

After the manifest exists, generate two HTML deliverables: one goal/taxonomy/case showcase with 10 reviewed cases per task, and one design-rationale/capability page. Any illustrative placeholder must carry a not_simulator_validated badge.
Correct the blackboard state by treating case_manifest_ready and showcase_ready as false until data_manifest-backed cases are reviewed.
Run M4, M5, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, floor-patch/corridor-width, VLM, M2b, and human sanity checks before making empirical claims.

risks.risk: Reviewers may dismiss the benchmark as wall-hit detection if T1/T5 dominate the paper narrative.
risks.mitigation: Lead with the T1/T2/T4 triad and present T3/T5 as coverage extensions.

risks.risk: Hidden or off-image geometry can silently determine labels, especially for T3 and T5.
risks.mitigation: Require visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and collision_point_visible when applicable.

risks.risk: Shortcut baselines may solve many cases without swept-volume reasoning.
risks.mitigation: Run blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, largest-floor-patch, and corridor-width heuristics before any claim.

risks.risk: T4 can be gamed by monotonic body-size priors if options always expose the smaller body.
risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include both-complete and neither-complete no-flip controls, and report pair consistency.

risks.risk: Simulator artifacts can create noisy labels around glass, thin structures, depth holes, overhangs, and movable objects.
risks.mitigation: Discard ambiguous cases and require RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, and ambiguity_reason for audit.

risks.risk: Body-width normalization helps but does not fully remove monocular scale ambiguity.
risks.mitigation: Keep fixed camera height in the demo and include human sanity, M2b sweep overlay, and M3 depth probes.

risks.risk: The answers below are illustrative and may be wrong for any real RGB frame until oracle metadata is attached.
risks.mitigation: Replace or verify every label from data_manifest.json before public release or model scoring.

risks.risk: T3 and T5 can require hidden or off-image geometry if sampled carelessly.
risks.mitigation: Keep only cases with fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, and requires_hidden_geometry=false.

risks.risk: T4 can be solved by monotonic body-size shortcuts if body order is fixed.
risks.mitigation: Randomize Body A/Body B order, include both/no-flip/neither controls, and score counterfactual pair consistency.

risks.risk: Prompt wording can leak answers if it describes gaps, obstacles, or passability.
risks.mitigation: Questions below state only body, action, and options; geometric explanation is confined to rationale.

risks.risk: Unpublishable benchmark if labels or examples remain template-authored rather than deterministic simulator outputs.
risks.mitigation: Block public claims until every case is generated from the swept-cylinder oracle with non-null visibility metadata and audit visualizations.

risks.risk: False novelty if the benchmark is solved by language priors or simple 2D heuristics.
risks.mitigation: Require blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, corridor-width, and largest-floor-patch baselines before claiming embodied reasoning.

risks.risk: Hidden-geometry leakage, especially for T3 turn-then-forward and T5 fixed passability.
risks.mitigation: Keep T3/T5 extension-only unless fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and decisive collision evidence is visible.

risks.risk: T4 can be gamed by monotonic body-size reasoning because the smaller body is usually the successful option.
risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include both/neither controls, score pair consistency, and require same-image flip_pair_id evidence.

risks.risk: Body-width normalization may still be too hard from monocular RGB without calibrated camera/height cues.
risks.mitigation: Run human sanity checks and M2b/M3 probes to separate visual scale limits from swept-volume reasoning failures.

risks.risk: Taxonomy may look borrowed from spatial-intelligence benchmarks if presented too broadly.
risks.mitigation: Use EgoConseq-specific readouts: forward extent, directional sweep comparison, action-sequence consequence, body intervention, visible passability.

risks.risk: Unvalidated text templates could be mistaken for benchmark cases in the HTML deliverables.
risks.mitigation: Block ready_for_showcase_review; require simulator-backed data_manifest fields and per-case review before any case is shown.

risks.risk: A live --runner codex HTML/design round would polish placeholders instead of producing evidence.
risks.mitigation: Route the next phase to pipeline_verify/case generation, producing data_manifest.json and visualization assets before HTML case pages.

risks.risk: T3 and T5 can leak hidden geometry or collapse into shortcut tasks.
risks.mitigation: Keep them extension-only and require fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and shortcut baseline checks.

risks.risk: T4 can be solved by monotonic body-size priors if body order and answer distribution are fixed.
risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include flip and no-flip groups, and score pair consistency by counterfactual_group_id.

risks.risk: False novelty if the benchmark is described as new collision geometry or broad spatial intelligence.
risks.mitigation: State that swept-cylinder collision is the label engine; novelty is single-frame ego-body action-consequence diagnosis.
